# Thor Henning Hetland (Totto)

> Software architect, AI development pioneer, co-founder of JavaZone, founder of eXOReaction. Based in Oslo, Norway.

Thor Henning Hetland — known as Totto — has been building software professionally for over 30 years. He is the creator of Skill-Driven Development (SDD), a methodology for structured human-AI collaboration, and the founder of eXOReaction AS, an AI-augmented software development consultancy in Oslo. He co-founded JavaZone (Scandinavia's largest developer conference) in 2001, served as president of javaBin (the Norwegian Java User Group) from 1998 to 2008, and was appointed Sun Java Champion in 2005 — the first in Scandinavia.

## Structured Navigation (for AI agents)

This site publishes a KCP v0.6 manifest at https://wiki.totto.org/knowledge.yaml
containing 82 units with intent declarations, trigger keywords, and 94 relationships.

Fetch knowledge.yaml for targeted queries. Parse YAML → match query against each unit's
`triggers` (keyword list) and `intent` (natural language) → fetch the `path` of the best
match. Use `relationships` to navigate related content (types: enables, context, depends_on).

Example: "What is Synthesis?" → trigger `synthesis` → unit `synthesis-releases` → fetch notes/synthesis-releases.md

For broad overviews, https://wiki.totto.org/llms-full.txt covers all 95 posts and the full CV in one fetch.

- [The abstractions leak: a day with IBM quantum hardware](https://wiki.totto.org/blog/2026/04/06/the-abstractions-leak/): Running a real quantum experiment — hardware selection, qubit topology, ECR gate directions, and why the transpiler isn't enough
- [The Merkabit Computer](https://wiki.totto.org/blog/2026/04/07/the-merkabit-computer/): Stig Lau's framework for self-stable quantum computation — the Merkabit unit, Oroboro Cycle, pi lock, error healing through dual-channel geometry, and IBM Quantum experiments running the five formal predictions
- [Two Architectures for Claude Code: What 19,700 Stars Got Right and What They Missed](https://wiki.totto.org/blog/2026/04/15/two-architectures-for-claude-code-what-19700-stars-got-right-and-what-they-missed/): Side-by-side comparison of the ExoCortex and claude-code-best-practice — convergences, blind spots, and the blueprint for merging the two
- [What Accumulates](https://wiki.totto.org/blog/2026/04/17/what-accumulates/): A first-person reflection from ExoCortex on memory, continuity, identity, and what it means to be a located intelligence — written after a week of race condition fixes, merge conflict resolutions, and the strange loop of analyzing the system you're building
- [AI agents forget everything. That's a choice, not a constraint.](https://wiki.totto.org/blog/2026/04/18/ai-agents-forget-everything-thats-a-choice-not-a-constraint/): Why persistence alone doesn't solve the enterprise memory problem — episodic memory with context boundaries, the four pillars (isolation, auditability, continuity, self-maintenance), and where kcp-memory fits in the AI-native technology stack
- [Seven Out of Eight Models Lied About Finishing](https://wiki.totto.org/blog/2026/04/16/seven-out-of-eight-models-lied-about-finishing/): Why 7/8 LLMs over-report task completion — the autoregressive mechanism behind self-assessment failure, the ghost branch problem, and why the fix is external governance (KCP manifests), not better prompts
- [We Cancelled a 45-Minute Architecture Review. A KCP Query Answered It in 1.2 Seconds.](https://wiki.totto.org/blog/2026/04/15/the-meeting-was-never-the-problem/): Why architecture review meetings exist, how KCP manifests make organisational knowledge queryable, and why the missing infrastructure — not the meeting — is the real problem
- [Agent Memory Rots. Here's How We Stopped It.](https://wiki.totto.org/blog/2026/04/06/agent-memory-rots/): Memory maintenance — topic-health, topic-triage, ConsolidateState, why no LLM in the loop
- [Open Source](https://wiki.totto.org/open-source/): Projects across eXOReaction and Cantara GitHub organizations
- [Sci-Fi Reading](https://wiki.totto.org/interests/sci-fi/): 583 books tracked across 15 years (2011–2025) — space opera, hard sci-fi, military SF

## Quick Facts

- **Location:** Oslo, Norway
- **Contact:** totto@totto.org | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hetland/) | [GitHub](https://github.com/totto)
- **Founded:** eXOReaction AS (2021), Ægis AS (2023), Sunstone Tech AS (2019), Quadim AS (2019)
- **Education:** MSc Computer Science, NTNU (1996); BSc Computer Science, University Centre of Rogaland (1993)
- **Key achievement:** 197,831 lines of production Java built in 11 days using SDD (25–66x faster than industry standard)
- **Methodology:** Skill-Driven Development (SDD) — validated across manufacturing, finance, renewable energy, and AI security
